Survey data

The planner shows only what this kind of data needs: the multibeam sensor and swath for bathymetry, the range and coverage for side-scan.

Coordinate system for imported files
No EPSG CRS loaded.

Lookups use epsg.io or spatialreference.org and are cached in this browser, so codes you have used work offline later. The full EPSG dataset is not embedded. Datum grid files (NTv2 etc.) are not supported.

Values in the grey boxes come from the selected system; choose Custom to edit them. Shifts use a 3-parameter Molodensky transform (about a metre).

Swath & overlap
Total swath width (W)-
Line spacing (S), at design depth-
Actual spacing (min – max, mean)-

Adaptive mode needs depth data: global bathymetry (section {§gbath}) or your own XYZ soundings (section {§xyz}). Each line is placed as far from the previous one as the local depth allows while keeping the chosen overlap along its whole length. The swath is assumed to see flat seabed at the depth under the line, and the lines alternate direction (port/starboard angles swap).

Coverage and gaps (infill)

Load what has been surveyed so far. The planner marks the covered parts of the area, finds the gaps (holidays) and plans infill lines across them.

Processed data (recommended)

No grid loaded.

GeoTIFFs in WGS 84 or WGS 84 / UTM are placed from their own EPSG code; other files use the coordinate system of section {§crs}. Use LZW, Deflate or no compression (not JPEG). Large files are read at reduced resolution.

Track lines (estimate before processing)

No tracks loaded.

From depth: the swath angles of section {§swath} and the depth along each track (loaded bathymetry, or the design depth). Port is left of the direction of travel.

Each track sees from the nadir gap under the towfish (about its height on each side) out to the range. At 200 %, every point must be seen by two tracks; points seen once show in yellow. Infill lines are spaced for the chosen coverage.

Grid and gaps

Everything inside the boundary that the loaded data does not cover is a gap: holes between tracks and the strips still missing along the edges. A margin outside the boundary counts too, so the swath edges reach past it; the coverage percentage is of the area itself.

Survey boundary import
Supported: SHP (+PRJ, or a ZIP), DXF, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, WKT, CSV/TXT vertex lists. Select the .shp and .prj together.

CRS: KML, KMZ, GPX and GeoJSON are WGS84 by specification. SHP uses its .prj file when present. DXF, WKT and text lists carry no CRS, so they use the coordinate system in section {§crs}. DWG is a closed binary format and cannot be read in a browser: save it as DXF first (AutoCAD, BricsCAD, ODA File Converter or LibreDWG). If several shapes are found, the largest closed one becomes the boundary.

Line direction
The main lines run parallel to one depth contour of the loaded bathymetry, offset at the design line spacing and cut to the area and to navigable water. On a sloping seabed each line then stays at about the same depth, so the swath stays even. The azimuth sets only the cross lines; adaptive spacing does not apply.
Williamson turn
Turning diameter (2R)-

If 2R > S an outward bulb (Williamson) turn is generated; otherwise a plain U-turn.

Project & operations (summary, cost and report)

Project details, sensor, IHO order, speed, vessel and coordinate system follow you to the other SwathPlan planners on this device; the survey area is shared between the MBES and geophysical planners.

The report is a self-contained HTML page with the map and all statistics. Open it and use Print → Save as PDF.

Map background & search

Google and Bing have no free keyless tile URL. Paste the tile URL from your own API account into Custom. Placeholders: {z} {x} {y}, {q} = Bing quadkey, {s} = subdomain a–c.

A PMTiles file is read in small pieces, so even a large file stays light on a phone. Convert MBTiles with the pmtiles tool, or download a file from a provider that allows offline use.

Map tiles you view are kept on this device for offline use. Before going offline, pan and zoom over your survey area at the scales you need.

Saves your Custom tile URL for the survey area. The built-in map servers do not allow bulk downloads.

Offline maps work on the website and in the installed app.

Coastline & land avoidance
No coastline loaded. Close an area first.

A loaded coastline is kept with the project, in the autosave and in saved .SPL files, so download the OSM coastline once while online and it keeps working offline. The OSM coastline is detailed and worldwide but user-contributed: check it against official charts. The built-in coastline is Natural Earth 1:10m, accurate to a few hundred metres (1:50m, about 1 km, when the page is used on its own without its data folder): fine for offshore and coastal planning, with a clearance to match, but not for harbours. For detailed offline work, load a GeoJSON export of GSHHG (full) or OSM land polygons. Turns that cross land or come within the clearance are flagged in the plan checks.

Bathymetry from XYZ file (your own data)

Horizontal coordinates use the system chosen in section {§crs}. Soundings loaded here replace any global data.

Export

Map sheet, PDF report and images

A hydrographic-style plan sheet with graticule, scale bar, north arrow, legend and title block. Printed at 100 % the scale bar is true.

One sheet per segment: PDFs get a page per segment, images one per sheet in a zip, DXF one file with each segment on its own layers and a named view per segment; other formats one file. One file per segment: every format is saved once per segment, with only that segment's lines, outline and statistics, all in one zip; map sheets and the report also get an overview. Whole route: one file, on one sheet.

GPX, KML, GML and NMEA are always WGS84 lat/lon. CSV, TXT, WKT, MIF and LNW follow the coordinate system chosen above. The HYPACK LNW layout is written from memory, so test-import it. DWG cannot be written from a browser: open the DXF in AutoCAD or BricsCAD and Save As DWG (or use ODA File Converter). The .LNX layout is written from memory of the HYPACK format; test-import before field use.

EIVA RLN follows the Helmsman runline format (E, N, KP). The Qinsy .qgfline file is rebuilt from a single sample file, so test-import it first. It uses WGS84 UTM (zone from the area centre) and straight lines only. Qinsy also reads DXF, DWG and KML.

Uncertainty budget (a priori TPU)

Enter the 1σ uncertainty of each part of the system. The planner combines them for every beam angle at the design depth and compares the 95 % result with the IHO S-44 order in section {§iho}.

A simplified a priori model after Hare (1995): range, angle (roll plus pointing), heave, water level, draft and sound speed for depth; positioning, heading, angle, pitch and sound speed for position. 95 % = 1.96σ vertical, 2.45σ horizontal. Check it against your own uncertainty model before you commit to a specification.

Compare scenarios (tender)

Save the current settings as a scenario, change what you want to compare (sensor, overlap, swath angle, speed, turn radius, day rate, working hours, vessels), and compare time, line length and cost on the same area or route.

Each scenario is planned with the same geometry and project settings as the planner. Days include the weather allowance, mob/demob and calibration from Project & operations. With several vessels the days are shared between them and each vessel is charged its own days.

Global bathymetry (online, free)
Close an area first (draw, preset or import), then fetch.

The data are only as good as the source: GMRT and NCEI hold real multibeam surveys in places but are 100–450 m grids elsewhere, so use them for planning, not as a substitute for your own soundings. Land and drying cells are ignored. Vertical datum is roughly mean sea level, not chart datum: use the vertical offset in section {§xyz} or choose a conservative depth. If your browser blocks a service (offline or CORS), use the link shown to download the grid and load it here. Sources: GMRT (Lamont-Doherty), NOAA NCEI, EMODnet, GEBCO via Open Topo Data (1 request per second, 1000 per day).
